text: The LIM-class homeo box gene Xlim-1, isolated from Xenopus laevis and related to lin-11 and mec-3, shows low mRNA in unfertilized eggs, peaks at gastrula, declines, rises in tadpoles, and is highest in adult brain, suggesting multiple developmental roles. In gastrulae, Xlim-1 mRNA localizes to the dorsal lip and dorsal mesoderm (Spemann's organizer); explants show synergistic induction by activin A and retinoic acid. Its structure and organizer-restricted expression suggest a role in establishing body pattern during gastrulation. Separately, IEX-1 is rapidly (30–60 min) induced by all-trans- or cis-RA in APL lines NB4 (PML–RARα) and KG1 (PLZF–RARα), independent of TNFα, NF-κB, and MAP kinases. In NB4, induction is transient and reversible, with cell cycle arrest, differentiation, and lower apoptotic sensitivity; in KG1 it persists for days with continued cycling and increased apoptotic sensitivity. Two functional RA-response elements were identified in the IEX-1 promoter.
